name: per-base-alignment-accuracy-assessment
description: Use when benchmarking long-read mappers (GraphMap, BWA-MEM, LAST, BLASR, DALIGNER, BLAST) on simulated Illumina/PacBio/ONT 1D/2D reads where the true genomic origin of every read is known and per-base alignment quality must be quantified.

name: per-base-coverage-computation-from-bam
description: Use when a BAM/CRAM (e.g., NA19240 nanopore reads aligned with NGMLR/minimap2/lra) must be converted into per-base or per-region coverage over SV intervals plus 1-Mb flanks for coverage-support analysis.

name: per-base-coverage-extraction-with-samtools-depth
description: Use when you have a BAM from mapping read subsets onto a specific reference FASTA and need the per-base covered fraction, gap identification, or coverage progression across iterative read-subset expansion cycles.

name: per-base-dwell-time-mse-optimization
description: Use when training or fine-tuning a nanopore signal simulator whose per-base signal levels must match resquiggle-derived dwell-time statistics for ONT DNA R10.4.1 or direct-RNA RNA004 chemistry.

name: per-base-pair-sensitivity-specificity-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking a peak caller for broad histone marks (e.g. H3K27me3) against a qPCR-validated truth set and needing threshold-free ROC comparison of sensitivity and specificity per base pair.

name: per-base-quality-profiling
description: Use when raw short-read data is supplied as FASTQ files and you need per-cycle quality summaries before or after preprocessing, especially for many samples requiring one combined visual QC report.

name: per-batch-sequencing-statistics-parsing
description: Use when monitoring a live nanopore sequencing run where FASTQ batches land incrementally and you need per-batch and cumulative QC metrics (reads, base pairs, classification rates) for a dashboard or QC table.

name: per-bin-summary-table-generation
description: Use when you have binned contig FASTA files from a metagenome assembly and need per-MAG quality metrics (contig count, N50, completeness, contamination) consolidated for bin selection.

name: per-biotype-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when you have a reserved test set of raw nanopore DRS signals with GENCODE-derived ground-truth gene/biotype labels and need per-biotype classification accuracy of a trained RISER model.

name: per-brick-interview
description: Run a focused interview with the operator about **one specific brick** (a feature, a module, a cross-cutting concern, a structural finding, an integration). Capture every answer in a durable transcript that other passes can read.

name: per-browser-developer-setting-navigation
description: Use when you are attempting to run a web application (such as COLMARvista) locally by opening index.html directly in a browser, the application uses WebWorker and/or WebAssembly components, and these fail to load due to default file-access policies.

name: per-building-infrastructure
description: Pattern for attaching infrastructure (canals, beacons, paths) to each building in the village

name: per-caller-sensitivity-counting
description: Use when comparing sensitivity of TE insertion callers (sTELLeR, TLDR, xTEA) on long-read BAMs by counting true positives against an assembly-based callset, as in the sTELLeR paper's Table 3.

name: per-category-modeling-backfire
description: Per-category/per-family models can produce WORSE leaderboard scores than a single global model, even when per-category CV is better. Use when: (1) Considering training separate models per product category/family/store in tabular competitions, (2) Per-category CV improves but LB degrades, (3) Each category has <100K rows from a larger dataset. Covers data volume thresholds, hybrid fallback strategies, and when per-category modeling is appropriate vs counterproductive.

name: per-cell-annotation-accuracy-computation
description: Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq cell-type annotation tools (e.g. EasyCellType vs Garnett, scPred, SingleR) on simulated datasets with known ground-truth labels and you need per-cell accuracy tables.

name: per-cell-annotation-table-export
description: Use when an imported single-cell study needs standardized, ontology-resolved cell type labels per individual cell so that cross-study expression comparisons in Cellenium are semantically integratable.

name: per-cell-bam-processing
description: Use when starting from per-cell (barcode-split) BAM files from a 10x or non-10x scRNA-seq experiment and you need a per-cell normalized gene body coverage vector for SkewC quality/skewness analysis.

name: per-cell-channel-intensity-quantification
description: Use when image-based spatial omics data (Xenium, CosMX, MACSima, PhenoCycler) contains protein-staining channels and per-cell intensity values are needed for cell-type annotation or niche enrichment analysis.

name: per-cell-compartment-marker-quantification
description: Use when a multiplexed imaging segmentation mask (e.g., from MIRIAM, MIBI or immunofluorescence TMA data) is available and per-cell, per-compartment marker intensity values are needed as a single-cell feature table.

name: per-cell-correlation-evaluation-against-reference-matrix
description: Use when evaluating a single-cell long-read isoform quantification method against a matched gold-standard count matrix, e.g. Nanopore output vs PacBio IsoSeq truth for the same Jurkat 5' cDNA library.

name: per-cell-fusion-call-summarization
description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., K562 Smart-seq2, SRP291312) has been run through fusion detectors per cell and calls must be aggregated per cell per tool for benchmarking.

name: per-cell-genotype-matrix-quantification
description: Use when 10x Chromium single-cell BAMs aligned with cellranger must be genotyped at a pre-called somatic variant set (e.g. from eWGS tumor/normal) to assign variant evidence to individual cell barcodes.

name: per-cell-informativeness-scoring
description: Use when a cell-typed .h5ad single-cell dataset is too large for ML/DL training and you need a per-cell importance score before sketching, or want to rank ambiguous/atypical cells by OOB accuracy.

name: per-cell-kl-divergence-quantification
description: Use when you need a local, per-cell quality measure for a 2D embedding (t-SNE or UMAP) — e.g. to feed EMBEDR p-value estimation, compare DR algorithms, or tune perplexity/n_neighbors.

name: per-cell-optimal-neighborhood-scale-selection
description: Use when an EMBEDR perplexity (or n_neighbors) sweep has been fit on scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq data and you want per-sample optimal scales, or a sample-wise optimal embedding, instead of a single global hyperparameter.

name: per-cell-pathogen-umi-quantification
description: Use when you have 10x scRNA-seq data from an infected sample for which cellranger count has already run against the host genome, and you need per-cell pathogen read and UMI counts appended to the 10x matrices for downstream single-cell analysis.

name: per-cell-prediction-table-generation
description: Use when scRNA-seq Seurat objects from tumor datasets (e.g. Massalha 2020, Peng 2019, Pelka 2021 liver/pancreatic/colon cohorts) need per-cell malignant classification and cell-of-origin labels compiled into one prediction table.

name: per-cell-qc-metrics-extraction
description: Use when two cellranger count runs on identical reads must be compared by per-cell QC summary statistics to quantify the effect of swapping the reference annotation (e.g. canonical vs. peaks2utr-augmented GFF3).

name: per-cell-regulator-activity-comparison-across-clusters
description: Use when you have a fitted scKINETICS model (GRN matrix A + per-cell velocities) and need TF-level, per-cell activity scores to identify regulators whose influence varies across clusters, e.g. acinar vs transitioning vs duct-like populations.

name: per-cell-signature-score-visualization
description: Use when per-cell annotation or disease scores (e.g., LHSC_per_cell_score, Neoplastic_monocyte_per_cell_score) are stored in a Seurat object's metadata and you need to compare their spatial/UMAP distributions across biological conditions such as healthy vs AML or diagnosis vs relapse.

name: per-cell-snv-genotyping-matrix-construction
description: Use when you have long-read (ONT/PacBio) amplicon reads from 10x Genomics 5' scRNA-seq cDNA libraries targeting known somatic mutations and need per-cell genotype calls and genotyping rates keyed by cell barcode.

name: per-cell-tei-computation
description: Use when an AnnData scRNA-seq object and a gene-age orthomap (e.g. from OrthoFinder/oggmap) are available and you need gene age-weighted expression summaries such as per-cell or per-stage TEI to test developmental hourglass patterns.

name: per-cell-type-accuracy-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when you have cell-type label predictions for query datasets mapped onto a pre-trained reference (e.g., scCobra KNN label transfer on GSE114297/GSE85247/GSE83312 pancreas queries) and need a per-cell-type accuracy breakdown, such as reproducing the Fig. 6b-e ACC heatmap.

name: per-cell-type-auroc-evaluation
description: Use when you have a pretrained Miscell latent feature matrix (e.g. from PBMC scRNA-seq) with known cell-type labels and need to quantify how well those features separate 7 cell types via a linear probe.

name: per-cell-type-confidence-aggregation
description: Use when comparing cell-type annotation quality between two representations of Visium HD data (e.g. bin2cell cells vs 8 μm bins) and you need per-cell-type tallies of median confidence and mean genes detected.

name: per-cell-type-density-estimation
description: Use when scRNA-seq cells carry per-cell activity scores (from ORIGINS2 activity()) plus known cell-type labels, and you need density distributions per type to compare biological programs across clusters.

name: per-cell-type-doublet-proportion-quantification
description: Use when Chord (or another doublet caller) has output predicted doublet barcodes for annotated scRNA-seq samples and you need per-sample doublet rates and per-cell-type doublet proportions to identify doublet-enriched populations.

name: per-cell-type-isoform-quantification
description: Use when you have PacBio/ONT single-cell long-read fastq.gz files plus a barcode-to-cell-type assignment table (e.g. from Seurat short-read analysis) and need per-cell-type isoform, TSS, or polyA counts.

name: per-cell-type-mean-expression-computation
description: Use when you have a labeled scRNA-seq reference matrix (cells × genes with cell-type annotations) and need cell-type-level mean expression vectors to feed the E-test ΔS gene-selection statistic or a multinomial MLE classifier.

name: per-cell-type-scaled-expression-differential-analysis
description: Use when a gene metagene or embedding-derived gene program must be validated as cell-type-independent by comparing per-cell scaled expression of its member genes between conditions (e.g., stimulated vs control) within each annotated cell type.

name: per-cell-umi-count-statistical-testing
description: Use when two 10x scRNA-seq libraries must be compared for equal per-cell capture depth (genes/UMIs per cell), e.g. fresh vs cryopreserved PBMCs, after matching mean reads per cell by downsampling.

name: per-cell-viral-read-count-aggregation
description: Use when you have per-sample pathogen_al_counts.csv files from scPathoQuant runs over a multi-virus reference (e.g. SARS-CoV-2 + metapneumovirus) and need to aggregate per-cell counts into a per-virus infected-cell and read-abundance table.

description: Add a per-chat configurable knob (spam_threshold, report_hour, captcha_difficulty) — migration → ChatConfig struct → API DTO → transactional update endpoint.

name: per-chromosome-genomic-array-io
description: Use when a pipeline needs to persist or reload per-chromosome, binned genomic annotation arrays (e.g. deepC skeleton tags in 1–10 range) from Hi-C contact maps at 5 kb resolution.

name: per-chromosome-phased-assembly
description: Use when you have a long-read WGS BAM (PacBio HiFi/CLR or ONT) from a diploid sample and need a phased, per-chromosome diploid assembly as input for SV calling or resource benchmarking.

name: per-class-bgc-similarity-tuning
description: Use when tuning BiG-SCAPE pairwise distance weights per BGC class, e.g. when JI/AI/DSS combinations must be optimized against MIBiG compound structural distances for classes like RiPPs or PKS/NRP hybrids.

name: per-class-f1-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking an annotation or classification model whose improvement is concentrated in minority classes, and aggregate metrics would hide the rare-class gains.

name: per-class-f1-score-computation
description: Use when you have predicted cell-type annotations from a tool like Census plus reference labels for the same cells and need per-class F1 scores, or need to test annotation robustness across embedding parameter grids.

name: per-class-f1-score-evaluation
description: Use when a galaxy/QSO/star classifier (e.g. SHEEP's XGBoost/LightGBM/CatBoost ensemble) has been trained on SDSS DR15+WISE photometry and you need per-class F1-scores to validate against the reported values or to run baseline/ablation comparisons.

name: per-class-f1-score-evaluation
description: Use when a multiclass or hierarchical cell-type classifier must be validated against labelled ground truth and reported per cell type, e.g. fivefold cross-validation on the pan-cancer training reference or the blood/stroma/cancer benchmark of Fig. 2c.

name: per-class-precision-recall-f1-computation
description: Use when you have a multiclass confusion matrix or class-level prediction counts and need to identify which class labels (e.g. NPClassifier superclasses) a model like DeepSAT predicts worst.

name: per-class-recall-performance-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing classifiers trained on different gene feature spaces over the five PAM50 subtypes, and you need per-class (subtype) recalls, macro-averaged recall, and precision on a held-out test split rather than aggregate accuracy alone.

name: per-class-sensitivity-specificity-evaluation
description: Use when a CMS prediction (or any 4-class sample-subtype assignment) must be validated sample-by-sample against original reference labels on a held-out cohort and per-class sensitivity/specificity are required, not just a single accuracy figure.

name: per-client-memory-router
description: Stops one agent working N clients from bleeding context between them, and stops N parallel client jobs from starving each other on the same model quota. Partition memory into a global store plus one isolated store per client, then gate execution through a concurrency-limited router so no single client's job queue can starve the rest. Use when one agentic setup serves multiple clients, when a client's context/preferences ever showed up in another client's output, or when parallel client jobs are timing out or burning quota unevenly.

name: per-clip-scene-research
description: Use when planning or generating any film clip: research similar cinema stills in the browser first, analyse the setup, then write the card. Never generate from adjectives or memory alone.

name: per-cluster-consensus-cnv-imputation
description: Use when per-cell CNV calls from scATAC-seq data are noisy or sparse and cluster-level consensus genotypes are needed — e.g. after identifyCNVClusters has produced a CNV cluster file and Louvain cell clusters exist.

name: per-cluster-interaction-count-aggregation
description: Use when you have pre-computed CCI datasets (e.g., CellPhoneDB output) for two or more conditions and want to identify cell clusters whose total interaction counts differ strikingly between conditions.

name: per-cluster-marker-ranking-by-ncdi
description: Use when analyzing a preprocessed Seurat object (e.g., Tyser 2021, 1195 cells) and the goal is cluster-specific binary markers — genes expressed exclusively in one cell population — rather than graded average-expression DE.

name: per-cluster-metric-aggregation
description: Use when a per-cell metric must be summarized per annotated cluster and globally to compare methods, e.g. local velocity inconsistency via mean cosine distance to k=30 neighbors across velocity methods.

name: per-cluster-metric-aggregation
description: Use when mapping a query single-cell dataset onto a Symphony reference and you need to detect query cell populations (clusters) that are absent from the reference, e.g. after holding out or ablating a cell type.

name: per-cluster-score-aggregation-and-thresholding
description: Use when a cell-by-cell-type score matrix (e.g. ScType es.max output on a clustered Seurat object) must be collapsed into one label per cluster, with a minimum-score threshold to flag unannotated clusters.

name: per-cohort-z-score-scaling

name: per-component-concentration-position-refinement

name: per-compound-majority-vote-aggregation
description: Use when a compound-level decision must be derived from multiple per-spectrum classifier outputs (e.g. EI-MS and ESI-MS/MS spectra of the same compound) and a single bitter/nonbitter label is required for precision/recall evaluation.

name: per-compound-match-table-compilation
description: Use when you have parsed MASST match records for a library of synthesized compounds and need to compile per-compound counts of matched public files and total matches, then reconcile totals against reported figures.

name: per-compound-spectrum-merging

name: per-contig-mapping-count-aggregation

name: per-contig-read-coverage-quantification
description: Use when validating metagenome assemblies by measuring what fraction of contig bases are covered by mapped reads — e.g. to detect poorly covered assembler outputs like the CLC bio Horizon oil-spill assembly (~85% coverage vs ~99% for MeGAMerge).

name: per-database-count-tabulation
description: Reference for adoptions/usage volumes of a chemical classification tool across named chemical databases (DrugBank, HMDB, ChEBI, PubChem, LIPID MAPS) — e.g. building an impact or adoption table for a classifier.

name: per-dataset-entry-tabulation

name: per-dataset-malignant-fraction-aggregation
description: Use when you have per-cell malignant-cell predictions from a scRNA-seq annotation model across many datasets and need to compare dataset-level malignant fractions against reference percentages (e.g., CancerSCEM database values).

name: per-dataset-metrics-table-assembly

name: per-dataset-summary-table-assembly

name: pericles-api-conventions
description: How API endpoints in Pericles validate input, shape responses, and enforce tenant scope. Use this WHENEVER you add or change an HTTP endpoint (Express auth-server or a Next.js route handler). Encodes the Zod request-validation pattern, the {success, data, metadata} response envelope, the canonical 10-risk-type enum, error shape, and the rule that organization_id is always validated server-side, never trusted from the client.

name: pericles-assessments-ui
description: How to build Assessments — the risk-profiling module: a Risk Profile heat map, report generation, a report viewer, and scenario exploration. Use this WHENEVER you build or change assessment frameworks, the heat map, report generation/viewing, or scenarios. Encodes the surfaces, reuse of the RiskAssessment model and ERP-derived context, pack-provided assessment types, persona data scope, and report distribution via an Execution Node.

name: pericles-atlas-mocker
description: How to give Atlas live-looking motion — moving vessel dots and progressing sea-route lines — for the investment/interest MVP, WITHOUT a paid carrier or AIS feed. Use this WHENEVER you build or change shipment position simulation, the ShipmentPositionFeed seam, voyage/route geometry, or the Atlas live vessel layer. The data under the motion is REAL (BOL-seeded suppliers, carriers, vessels, lanes); only position-over-time is synthesized, behind one interface that swaps to real Terminal49 + AISstream data with a config flip.

name: pericles-atlas-ui
description: How to build Atlas — the Google-Maps-style operational picture of suppliers, shipments, routes, and events. Use this WHENEVER you build or change the map, its layers, clustering, the filter bar, the events feed, or Atlas defaults. Encodes the Google Maps parity bar (map+satellite, smooth zoom/pan), the supplier/shipment/route/ event layers with route progress, the full filter set, and Industry-Pack-driven defaults.

name: pericles-compliance-audit
description: How Pericles stays doctrine-compliant over time — the §11 compliance cadence and the §12 ADR process. Use this WHENEVER you run a PR doctrine check, prepare an architecture review, conduct the quarterly audit, set audit-log retention, pin versions, or author an ADR / file a carve-out exception. Encodes the three compliance checkpoints, the immutable-log + retention rules, and the ADR template.

name: pericles-copilot-ui
description: How to build the persistent Co-Pilot — the cross-pipeline assistant present across Pericles. Use this WHENEVER you build or change the Co-Pilot surface, its streaming, its action proposals, or the gateway-path affordance. Encodes the persistent surface, persona framing, the §4 cross_pipeline + audited gateway-path UX, and the §3 rule that Co-Pilot proposes while Execution Nodes commit.

name: pericles-cross-customer-learning
description: How to activate cross-customer learning — the §9 Phase 2 step that turns per-tenant signal into aggregated platform intelligence WITHOUT letting any customer-identifying context leave a tenant. Use this WHENEVER you build the aggregation pipeline, the differential-privacy budget, or surfaces that consume aggregated insight. Encodes the Phase 1 (extract) / Phase 2 (aggregate) split, per-tenant DP budgets, halt-on- exhaustion, and the prohibition on identifying context ever leaving a tenant.

name: pericles-custom-skill
description: How customers (and partners) author Custom Skills that extend Pericles for their tenant — without forking the platform or escaping the sandbox. Use this WHENEVER you build the Custom Skill authoring/review/runtime surfaces, define the sandbox, or review a Custom Skill for activation. Encodes §8 extend-never-override, tenant- namespace binding, the four-stage review, the sandbox constraints (MCP-only egress, no direct DB, allow-listed libs, no direct Execution Node), and lifecycle.

name: pericles-customer-onboarding
description: How to onboard a CUSTOMER into Pericles end-to-end from public bill-of-lading data: create the parent company and all its branded subsidiaries as Organizations with their business info, pull each subsidiary's shipments, carriers, and suppliers from ImportYeti via Apify, and seed BOTH the relational Supplier/Carrier/Shipment tables (the path Atlas + the position mocker read) and the OrganizationContext rollup (the path monitoring reads). Use this WHENEVER you onboard a trial/customer, wire the ImportYeti→Apify scrape, build the BOL→table seeder, or change how a tenant's org hierarchy and suppl…

name: pericles-data-model
description: How to model data in Pericles with Prisma + PostgreSQL. Use this WHENEVER you add or change a table, a query, or a migration. Encodes the real schema: organization_id on every tenant table, the Event(validation_status) → Incident lifecycle, EventHash TTL dedup, the MonitoringAuditLog/AuthAuditLog audit tables, the MessageQueue + KeyValueStore infrastructure tables, UserOrganization RBAC, and the Organization hierarchy where branded subsidiaries are child orgs — no Kafka, no Redis.

name: pericles-deployment-shapes
description: How Pericles ships as three deployment shapes — Express, Standard, Enterprise — on one engine (§7). Use this WHENEVER a feature differs by shape: tenancy, configuration, auth/SSO, governance, audit access, pack upgrades, or Custom Skills. Encodes what varies (topology, governance, admin surface) and what NEVER varies (the engine and the Skills), so you never fork the codebase per shape.

name: pericles-dev-environment
description: How to set up and work in the Pericles dev environment — docker-compose services, the .env.local convention, the canonical npm scripts (dev:all, monitoring:start, prisma, mocker, jobs:cleanup), and the pre-commit gate. Use this WHENEVER onboarding a developer, adding a service, or wiring CI. Encodes the existing docker-compose (postgres, pgadmin), the dotenv-from-repo-root pattern, and the mandatory lint + type-check before merge.

name: pericles-doctrine
description: The keystone skill for building Pericles. Use this WHENEVER you are about to add or change an agent, a Skill manifest, a data integration, an Execution Node, or any architectural decision in the Pericles codebase — even if the change seems small. It encodes the Platform Doctrine (§1–§12) in operational form: how to stay doctrine-compliant, the PR "doctrine touched" checklist, and whether a departure needs an ADR or a §12 carve-out exception. Every other pericles-* skill assumes this one.

name: pericles-erp-adapter
description: How to build an ERP adapter that turns a customer's ERP into Pericles OrganizationContext. Use this WHENEVER you add or change an ERP integration (SAP S/4HANA exists; Dynamics 365, Epicor Kinetic, Infor CloudSuite are Wave 1). Encodes the adapter anatomy (client, types, transformer, sync-service, mock), the mapping to OrganizationContext, real-time ERP tools, mock mode, and that new adapters belong behind MCP (§5) while the SAP one is grandfathered.

name: pericles-evals-scorers
description: How to write Mastra scorers and gate Skills on them in Pericles. Use this WHENEVER you create or modify a scorer, promote a Skill toward published, or investigate a quality regression. Reflects the real createScorer API (@mastra/core/scores) with an LLM judge + preprocess, the three existing scorers in monitoring-scorer.ts, the no-eval-no-publish rule, the promotion gate, and drift detection.

name: pericles-execution-node
description: How to build deterministic Execution Nodes that commit consequential actions — the §3 "supervisors propose, executors commit" boundary. Use this WHENEVER an LLM-driven Skill would otherwise send a notification, commit freight, contact a supplier, message a customer, or write an audit record. Encodes the deterministic-commit rule, per-commit logging, trial vs run mode, and how this maps onto the existing Workflow node-handler engine (BaseNodeHandler + TRIGGER/ACTION/CONDITION/NOTIFICATION/END).

name: pericles-external-feeds
description: How to integrate external data feeds (NOAA, GDELT, NVD, FRED, WHO/CDC, TheNewsAPI, X/Twitter, MarineTraffic, etc.) the Pericles way. Use this WHENEVER you add or change an external API call in a monitoring tool or a new feed. Encodes the timeout + UA convention, treating every response as untrusted, API-key handling, and the rule that new feeds go behind MCP while the existing inlined integrations are grandfathered.

name: pericles-frontend-foundations
description: The frontend foundation for Pericles — stack, structure, component pattern, state, realtime, and the "intuitive, no onboarding" + accessibility bar. Use this WHENEVER you build or change any UI (a page, component, store, or provider) in frontend/. Encodes Next.js 16 App Router + React 19, Tailwind + Radix/shadcn-style ui, zustand stores, socket.io-client realtime, the existing component layout, and persona framing via the Persona Layer.

name: pericles-functional-agent
description: How to build a Functional Agent/Skill and declare its pipeline position. Use this WHENEVER you create or modify a Mastra agent (Monitoring, Validation, Impact Assessment, Summarization, or a new one) or set a Skill's data_access.pattern. Encodes the §4 pre_validation / post_validation / cross_pipeline rules, the audited gateway path, and how the four design-level agents map to those positions. Misclassifying pipeline position is a doctrine violation.

name: pericles-industry-pack
description: How to assemble, version, and ship an Industry Pack — Pericles' unit of go-to-market. Use this WHENEVER you compose a Pack, write a Pack manifest, or decide what ships in a sector bundle. Encodes the eight pack elements, the versioned Pack manifest (which references Skill/template/adapter versions, never embeds them), pack versioning, the draft→published "three live customers" gate, and the forbidden list. A Pack is a product line, not a feature.

name: pericles-industry-skill
description: How to author an Industry Skill — the category-defining Skill that gives a sector its context, supplier-dependency reasoning, and disruption-duration estimation. Use this WHENEVER you build or version an Industry Skill (Industrial Manufacturing and High-Tech are Wave 1). Encodes what an Industry Skill provides, how it composes sector-weighted Topicals and reference data, its pipeline role, and the lifecycle gate (draft until the pack has three live customers).

name: pericles-intelligence-ui
description: How to build the Intelligence surface — the events feed, event/incident detail, the Insights chat with document viewer, and generated briefs/memos. Use this WHENEVER you build or change the events feed, an event sub-page, the Insights conversational view, or brief/memo generation. Encodes the feed, the chat + document viewer, persona framing, and that consequential outputs (e.g. sending a memo) go through Execution Nodes.

name: pericles-mastra-tool
description: How to author a Mastra createTool the Pericles way — the substrate every Skill formalizes. Use this WHENEVER you write or modify a tool in backend/src/mastra/tools: it covers the id/description, Zod input & output schemas, the execute({ context }) signature, the REQUIRED organization_id input field validated inside execute, the AbortSignal.timeout(10000) convention, and scorer wiring. A correctly built tool is a proto-Skill manifest, so doing this right makes the later registry lift trivial.

name: pericles-mcp-layer
description: How to access data through MCP — the target data-access layer for Pericles (§5). Use this WHENEVER you add a NEW data source (ERP, vector store, knowledge graph, external feed) or design how a Skill reaches data. Encodes the "new sources via MCP, existing inline grandfathered" rule, portability (swap stores behind MCP), audit symmetry (MCP access logged like any invocation), and tenant scoping enforced at the MCP boundary. .mcp.json holds exactly one server today (apify-importyeti) — this layer is still close to greenfield.

name: pericles-mobile
description: How to build Pericles mobile — the on-the-go surface that lets a Risk Manager or Supply Chain Manager triage events, approve actions, and consume briefs from a phone. Use this WHENEVER you scope or build mobile views. Encodes mobile-first persona framing, what subset of surfaces is in scope (read + approve, not full authoring), tenant scoping, and that approvals route through the same Execution Node + approval gate as web.

name: pericles-monitoring-pipeline
description: How the monitoring pipeline detects, deduplicates, filters, scores, and persists events. Use this WHENEVER you change detection, the content-hash dedup, the Haversine geo filter, severity/confidence scoring, the candidate→Validation hand-off, or the per-org monitoring process. Encodes the real pipeline in backend/src/monitoring and the 13 tools, the SHA-256 event hash, EventHash TTL, and that the Validation Agent step is currently a stub.

name: pericles-notifications
description: How to deliver platform notifications (email, SMS, Slack, Teams) reliably and safely. Use this WHENEVER you send an alert/notification, build a delivery channel, or handle retries. Encodes dispatch via the MessageQueue, delivery through the deterministic NotificationHandler (trial vs run mode), retries with backoff (attempts/max_attempts), and the rule that external communications are never auto-sent without an Execution Node and approval gate.

name: pericles-observability
description: How Skill invocations are logged, traced, and operated in Pericles. Use this WHENEVER you add an invocation path, emit logs, build a dashboard, or need lineage for "why did the platform do X". Reflects the existing instrumentation (MonitoringAuditLog, Mastra observability/AI tracing, PinoLogger, monitoring/metrics + error-reporter, socket.io realtime) and the target per-invocation lineage schema that extends it.

name: pericles-org-memory
description: How to build Organizational Memory — the customer's persistent context (documents, strategic customers/product lines, history) behind MCP, plus the §9 per-tenant cross-customer signal. Use this WHENEVER you ingest customer data, build retrieval (vector / knowledge graph), or design the privacy-preserving learning signal. Encodes ingestion + injection screening, vector+graph behind MCP, retrieval scoping, and the differential-privacy signal (OM Phase 1). Mostly net-new; OrganizationContext is the structured ERP slice that exists today.

name: pericles-partner-marketplace
description: How partners (consultancies, ERP integrators, regional resellers) author, list, and sell Skills on Pericles — extending Custom Skill mechanics across tenants. Use this WHENEVER you build the marketplace, partner publishing, partner-scoped review, or partner activation surfaces. Encodes that partner Skills are still Custom Skills with tenant binding, the four-stage review applies per tenant, partner-published Skills are not platform Skills (no override of platform IDs), and commercial mechanics are out of scope (GTM-owned).

name: pericles-persona-layer
description: How to build the Persona Layer that frames Skill outputs per user persona — WITHOUT forking agents per persona (§6). Use this WHENEVER output should differ for the Global Risk Manager vs Supply Chain Manager vs Business Stakeholder, or when you're tempted to branch a prompt/agent by role. Encodes the four persona dimensions (output shape, data scope, default module, vocabulary), the three real personas, and the rule that one substantive answer is rendered per persona.

name: pericles-plans-ui

Encodes the existing Workflow engine substrate (Workflow/Node/Edge/ Execution + handlers + reactflow), trial-mode simulation, and that execution commits through deterministic node handlers.

name: pericles-postgres-queue

Use this WHENEVER you need a job queue, background processing, scheduled work, notification dispatch, inter-agent messaging, rate limiting, or a cache/KV store, and ALWAYS push back when Kafka, Redis, RabbitMQ, Bull, or Celery is proposed. Reflects the existing MessageQueue model + monitoring/queue-client.ts and the KeyValueStore model.

name: pericles-predictive
description: How to build the predictive layer — forward-looking risk forecasts that complement the detect→validate→act pipeline. Use this WHENEVER you build forecasting Skills, surface predicted events, or compose historical signal + Org Memory + (post-§9-Phase-2) aggregated intelligence. Encodes that predictive Skills are pre_validation Functional Skills, must be evaluated against actual outcomes, and never commit actions on a prediction alone (proposals only, Execution Nodes commit).

name: pericles-prompts
description: How to author prompts safely in Pericles. Use this WHENEVER you write or modify a system prompt, prompt fragment, or any place where customer documents or external API content enters an LLM call. Encodes untrusted-content boundary marking, output-schema validation as an injection guard, cross-Skill contagion prevention, capability minimization, and persona-aware framing. Customer docs and external feeds are untrusted by default.

name: pericles-regional-skill
